title: Make packaged desktop startup safe from orphaned provider descendants
primary_claim: A provider descendant left behind by a crashed desktop cannot block the next packaged Daedalus launch or silently survive an orderly desktop shutdown.

invariants: bounded effects and explicit execution-limit exception

baseline.windows_failures: four identical BEX64 failures, exception 0xc0000409, FAST_FAIL_FATAL_APP_EXIT, offset 0x34b5f5
baseline.orphan: llama-server.exe PID 31256 had no live parent and loaded VCRUNTIME140.dll plus VCRUNTIME140_1.dll from the copied desktop backend
baseline.copy_failure: the stable backend destination rejected exclusive write access while the orphan held both DLL image mappings
baseline.backend_log: no new backend log entry was written by the failing launches
baseline.immediate_recovery: the exact orphan was terminated after path, parent absence, and both module locks were revalidated; both DLLs then became exclusively writable

acceptance: desktop-owned local Ollama starts from an explicit mutable service directory that contains no packaged runtime DLLs
Windows local Ollama is assigned to one kill-on-close Job Object before it can serve model work; assignment failure terminates the child and refuses managed startup
orderly close and the local Ollama stop route terminate the owned process tree, while a pre-existing reachable Ollama service remains unowned and untouched
the sidecar build emits one deterministic SHA-256 bundle identity and the native host is compiled against that exact identity
the sidecar emits a canonical exact-file manifest; unlisted files left by an overlay installer are neither trusted nor copied into a runtime generation
a bundle identity mismatch is refused before copying or spawning
each backend bundle is installed once through a private staging directory into an immutable identity-named generation; an existing generation is validated and never overwritten
only the allowlisted desktop state paths are copied from the previous active or legacy generation into a new generation, missing targets only, with links and type conflicts refused
the active-generation marker changes only after nonce-authenticated readiness succeeds and old generations are retained for rollback
desktop setup errors are written to a stable startup log and produce a non-zero exit without a Rust panic abort
release hashing keeps its one-megabyte I/O buffer off the Windows GUI thread stack and path policy follows Windows case-insensitive alias semantics
the frozen sidecar dispatches multiprocessing worker arguments before its Web API argument parser
focused Python contract/runtime tests, native Rust tests, and two packaged Windows starts with a resident Ollama model pass on this host

evidence.native_build: Tauri 2.11.4 release and NSIS bundle passed
evidence.installed_upgrade: NSIS overlay install exited 0; 63 observed stale resource files were not copied into the active generation
evidence.live_restart: two nonce-ready starts returned HTTP 200 with the same active identity and no additional generation
evidence.provider_modules: resident llama-server loaded zero modules from the install resource or app-data backend generation
evidence.orderly_shutdown: native host, frozen backend, Ollama, and llama-server all exited; port 8765 was free
evidence.retained_negative_evidence: startup log retains the pre-fix full-tree mismatch and CRLF-manifest parser failures

rollback: revert the scoped source and tests together
retain this packet, WER identifiers, and the orphan-process finding as negative startup evidence
do not delete legacy or identity-named backend generations during rollback
